assign.request: go through all the pages in this framework, and think, "how would i build this with a ui?" if we want to move pages to pure .json, how can the ui go from "new page" to any of the pages we have. top tabs? left sidebar tabs? column pages? header? footer? takeover? swap? color? etc... it needs to be better... simpler... more configurable. what's the ux for adding tabs to a page? what's the ux for configuring tabs?

log.msg: CENSUS - 890 page.js found under public/, 890 rows classified, the two numbers agree. TIERS: 197 pure configuration today (22%), 378 one named renderer away (42%), 315 code (35%).

CENSUS reasons that force code: a live control 137 - content computed from data 94 - async/fetch 53 - its own state 15 - a class of its own 16. Reasons that only need a NAME in the JSON: a house factory 268 - a page class (Template/Shell/Post/Scene/...) 79 - its own stylesheet 27 - fields from a helper 4.

CENSUS navigation: none 464 - columns 274 - top tabs 63 - left rail 27 - takeover 27 - right rail 20 - footer 11 - swap 4. Surface: plain 877, card 7, tint 2, prim 2, dark 2. Layout: 1.measure 661, 4.wall 144, 1.stack 64, 1.sections 18, 4.quarters 2, 3.thirds 1. Kind: prose 633, demo 118, wall 113, form 24, media 2.

CENSUS headline finding: there is NO small set of house factories to build renderers for. 817 distinct factory names across the corpus, 322 of them inside the 268 pages that are one word away, and the single biggest (dashboard) unlocks 16 pages; twelve greedy picks reach only 93 of 268. So the builder ships a CODE ESCAPE, not a renderer library.

CENSUS: crumbs is not a per-page choice at all - core draws the trail on the columns HOST after every activation (Page.reveal_column), so a builder cannot offer it per page. /imagine/layouts/ added the only switch and it belongs to the host.

assign.now: proved: 1280 and 3440, four widths, zero console errors - writing the landing

log.msg: PROTOTYPE /imagine/paging/build/ - seven controls (name, navigation, surface, layout, blocks, pages, code), the page assembling live in the middle, its page.json on the right. Three-track grid measured 297/542/371 at 1280 and 416/2398/480 at 3440; the two side tracks cap at min(24%,26rem) and min(30%,30rem) so the stage takes everything 3440 has spare. Stage and file panes are sticky.

PROVED headless: built a page with top tabs at 1280, saved through Make's FileStore, reloaded, still there; public/imagine/paging/made/built-with-the-builder/page.json and two child dirs on disk; opened cold at /imagine/paging/make/built-with-the-builder/ and the Router walked five columns. Switched navigation to columns and the same two blocks re-rendered as rows. At 3440 the stage rect was [488,89,2398,277] before a swap and identical after - url never changed. Zero console errors at 400/1280/1600/1920/3440.

FOUR TRAPS met while building, each measured: Page.naming() is core's url-deriving method and overriding it 404'd the whole page; Paging.chips() is called by dress() on every render; .cols is display:flex in @layer util and beat the sheet's display:grid (card shipped as 2 columns); a child's top-level default:true was silently dropped by FileStore.file() and had to move into mode. Also: pre is a dark code block in this theme, so overriding only its background left #e6e6e6 ink on a near-white box - the JSON pane read as an empty grey rectangle in three screenshots.

FOUR PROPOSALS, diffs in doc/builder.md, none applied (fences): (1) add `build` to paging/page.js children: - one word, and without it the builder is unreachable from the site; (2) blocks at the top level of a node, two lines in make/made.js; (3) Make draws a node's blocks, one line in make/page.js grow(); (4) register the `build-` prefix in framework/styles/css-scopes.txt.

Found outside the fence: baseline.js's mark renders its markdown at 3207px at 3440 - the nested p inside span.baseline-words escapes .page-column-prose's direct-child measure cap. One selector in baseline.css.

assign.outcome:
**The page builder landed, and the census that decided its shape.** Seven controls on the left, the page assembling live in the middle, its `page.json` on the right — and Save writes a real directory through Make's own store.

![](builder-1280.png)

**The census — 890 `page.js` found, 890 rows classified, the two numbers agree.**

| tier | pages | |
|---|---:|---|
| **configuration** | **197 (22%)** | a title, prose, children, a card wall. The builder writes this today. |
| **one word away** | **378 (42%)** | the page must NAME something js supplies — the `"kids": "tabs"` pattern. |
| **code** | **315 (35%)** | a live control (137) · content computed from data (94) · async/fetch (53). |

The finding that decided the builder: **there is no small set of house factories worth building renderers for.** 817 distinct factory names; the biggest single one unlocks 16 pages, and twelve greedy picks reach 93 of 268. So control 7 is a **code escape** — the `page.js` a hand would write, with the line where your code goes already marked.

**The controls, in order:** name · **navigation** · surface · layout · blocks · pages · code. Navigation is ONE control with six pictures — none, columns, top tabs, left rail, right rail, takeover — because top tabs, left tabs and column pages are one question asked once. Each writes a pair of words that already exist: `kids` (how children are drawn) and `mech` (what a click does). And `swap` is not offered: a swap with a bar is a tab strip, so the builder calls it tabs.

**Tabs, in plain words.** *A tab is a child page.* You add a page and pick “top tabs”; nothing else exists to create. *Configuring a tab is the four things every child has* — name, order, default, icon — which are the four controls on its row, each writing one field.

**Proved headless.** Built with top tabs at 1280 → saved → reloaded → still there; `made/built-with-the-builder/page.json` plus two child dirs on disk; opened cold at its own url and the Router walked five columns to it. Switched to columns and the same two blocks re-rendered as rows. At 3440 the stage rect read `[488, 89, 2398, 277]` before a swap and identical after, url unchanged. Zero console errors at 400 / 1280 / 1600 / 1920 / 3440; no overflow, nothing at x:0, prose capped at the measure.

**Four proposals, diffs in the doc, none applied (fences).** The first is one word and everything else depends on it: `build` in `paging/page.js`'s `children:` — without it the builder is unreachable from the site. Then `blocks` at the top level of a node (two lines in `make/made.js`), Make drawing a node's blocks (one line), and the `build-` prefix in `css-scopes.txt`.

**Left open, with reasons.** No “open an existing page to edit it” — that is `made.load()` plus a picker, and a half-built loader would have shipped without the reload proof; Make is where a made page is renamed and deleted. Blocks are edited in the controls, not in the stage, so the stage stays a picture of the file. And `baseline.js` renders its mark at 3207px at 3440 (a nested `p` escapes core's direct-child measure cap) — one selector, another task's file.

Start over had to CLEAR the store rather than apply(NEW_PAGE()): applying kept a fresh draft, so the amber mark never went away on a page that was back at its baseline.

FIFTH PROPOSAL, found at landing: /imagine/paging/doc/page.js landed the same night with a RECORDS map naming the four docs it knows about, so doc/builder.md is invisible on that wall until it is named - a two-line entry, in doc/builder.md's proposals. Every link the builder carries uses the raw .md path, which works either way.
